transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-31
Start: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Alex Morgan (Redwood AE), Jordan Kim (Redwood SE), Tara Nguyen (CSM) - Redwood; Priya Desai (Infra), Liam O'Connor (Platform), Sofia Ruiz (Security), Ben Chu (SRE) - AcmePayments
Notes/Links: Security pack link: https://redwood.example.com/secpack/ACME (placeholder), shared perf sheet: drive.google.com/notes/perf-acme (placeholder)

[00:00] Alex (Redwood): hey everyone, happy new year eve, thanks for joining this quick weekly, we'll cover networking updates, the upgrade schedule to the private runtime v1.8 and the perf runs — hi priya, liam
[00:18] Priya (Acme): hey alex, hi jordan, quick one — we finished mapping the subnets, we have two private subnets per AZ and a public for NLB, but we need clarity on the routing requirements for the control plane egress to pull model blobs
[00:38] Jordan (Redwood): yeah, good question — so for the private deployment the control plane needs outbound access to our model registry S3 buckets, it's just HTTPS egress, you can either NAT through a managed NAT gateway or allow egress via a controlled proxy; we sent the runbook but i'll reattach it after this call
[00:58] Liam (Acme): are there any IP allowlist ranges? we don't want to open everything, we'd prefer specific FQDNs or CIDR ranges
[01:14] Jordan: we recommend FQDN+SNI allowlist, but for some customers we provide a small range of egress IPs you can route to, i'll add that detail to the runbook — note that if you want cross-account peering there is an IAM role swap for the model pull step
[01:38] Sofia (Security): also wanted to confirm KMS around secrets, we need HSM-backed keys if possible and audit logs for key usage, is that supported in the private deployment?
[01:52] Alex: yes, you can point to your KMS (we support AWS KMS + BYOK via customer-managed policies), and audit logs are emitted to the control plane, we can stream audit events to your S3 bucket or CloudWatch — jordan will walk through the sample logs
[02:12] Jordan: (mumbles) sample logs are, uh, attached, warning: the auto-transcription might say K V cash in one place — it's kv cache, not k v cash, sorry speaker 1 — but the logs show key usage and model version pulls
[02:40] Ben (Acme): small note on routing, we saw a failover issue last week where NLB didn't preserve source IPs causing our firewall rules to kick, any suggestions?
[02:56] Jordan: yes that's likely the proxy/NLB idle timeout and the target group config, we recommend preserving client ip via proxy protocol v2 for TCP mode, for HTTP we recommend X-Forwarded-For. Also ensure cross-AZ targets are registered to avoid AZ-blast effects
[03:20] Priya: ok, on the perf side, we ran the 4-concurrent client test with 2k context and avg tokens/sec looked fine but p95 latency spiked at high concurrency — we suspect the KV cache warmup or batching behavior
[03:38] Jordan: that matches what we've seen. in v1.8 we shipped improved batching heuristics and a more aggressive prefix/KV cache retention policy. the KV cache warmup can cause p95 blips on cold starts, but sustained traffic should stead-state and p95 should drop, i'll run an 8k context test as requested
[04:01] Liam: does the upgrade to v1.8 require any downtime? what's the rollback plan?
[04:12] Alex: we planned a rolling upgrade with canary subsets: we upgrade a small pool, run smoke checks, then proceed; worst case rollback is to pin the previous model-serving kernel and redeploy the older runtime. we'll document the exact steps in the upgrade runbook and propose a maintenance window
[04:36] Sofia: please include the security validation checklist in that runbook — we need to ensure audit logs, key usage, and networking checks are covered before we greenlight the upgrade
[04:50] Jordan: absolutely, checklist will include: KMS key test, model pull test, request signing verification, RBAC sanity, and audit log ingest verification
[05:05] Alex: quick recap of perf numbers we need from you — p50/p95 for 2k and 8k context, concurrency levels 1/4/8, and a sample of token throughput; priya, can you run the 8k context test this week?
[05:22] Priya: yes i'll run it, probably tomorrow, but i need the exact test harness you ran — is that the /perf/run script in the shared drive?
[05:30] Jordan: yes that's right, i'll drop a step-by-step with the exact flags, for 8k context set --max_seq 8192 --batch 1 --concurrency 4 and enable kvcache profiling flag, the script will produce p50/p95 and the KV cache hit rate
[05:50] Ben: when you say kvcache profiling flag, is that intrusive? like will it change perf characteristics?
[05:58] Jordan: minor overhead (~2-3%), but it helps us see warmup behavior and cache hit/hit-miss ratios — we usually run one profiling pass then a clean run, we'll note which results are profiled
[06:10] Liam: anything on the SLOs? we're trying to map Redwood's p95 latency to our internal SLO of 500ms for common requests, are those achievable on private with our current instance types?
[06:24] Jordan: depends on model size and instance type; for the smaller 7B-ish models p95 of ~200-300ms is typical, for larger ones and 8k context you'll see higher latencies. we'll provide the performance profile table for your chosen model variants and recommended instance families in the runbook
[06:44] Priya: about network egress and cost — if the control plane pulls models during scale-up that could trigger egress charges, can we pre-warm caches with a local mirror?
[06:56] Alex: yes you can stage model artifacts in a customer S3 bucket and point the runtime to that mirror to avoid cross-region egress. that's in the docs but we can give an example policy and presigned workflow
[07:14] Sofia: also need clarification on audit retention — how long are logs kept in Redwood control plane by default and can we extend/ship them out?
[07:26] Tara (CSM): default retention is 30 days in the hosted telemetry; for private we surface logs to your storage so you control retention, we'll add a note in the secpack about retention and retention configuration steps
[07:40] Alex: ok shifting to upgrade schedule — proposed window 2027-01-10 01:00-05:00 UTC, tentative — does that work?
[07:52] Liam: that time works for our ops team, but we want a 2-hour canary phase first not the full 4h, can you do 2h canary then ramp?
[08:04] Jordan: yep we can. we'll do 2h canary on a small pool, smoke tests, then 2h ramp if green — rollback immediate if anomalies detected
[08:18] Priya: how will we be notified if rollback triggers? pager? slack?
[08:24] Alex: both: we will send a high-priority slack alert to your ops channel plus page the on-call SRE. We'll also open a ticket in your incident system if configured
[08:40] Ben: quick question on NLB health checks — we saw a pattern where idle connections were dropped causing the runtime to declare unhealthy, what's the right timeout?
[08:52] Jordan: set the NLB idle timeout to 350s and make sure the healthcheck is an HTTP 200 to /healthz with a 5s timeout, and set deregistration delay to 300s to allow in-flight requests to drain
[09:10] Priya: thanks, we'll update that. on the perf test I wanted to call out one weirdness: p95 spiked only on model switch during sharding, we think it's the kernel selection path
[09:24] Jordan: kernel selection can add overhead during the first sequence length jump — v1.8 has some improvements to cache pre-warming and kernel reuse, that should reduce model-switch spikes
[09:36] Alex: ok wrapping into action items, jordan will run the 8k perf and share results, i'll send the updated security runbook with IP ranges and upgrade steps
[09:48] Sofia: please ensure the runbook includes an explicit checklist for SOC2 reviewers — we will run an internal review as soon as we have the artifacts
[10:00] Alex: noted. anything else before we close?
[10:06] Liam: one last ask — can Redwood provide a small synthetic load test we can run from our env to validate cross-AZ failover? maybe a kubernetes job we can apply?
[10:18] Jordan: yes we have a k8s e2e job in the perf repo, i'll add instructions for deployment and a sample manifest, we'll also include sample logs to look for
[10:30] Priya: cool, i'll kick off the tests after lunch and share results in the perf sheet
[10:36] Alex: awesome thanks everybody, recap in slack and i'll follow up with attachments and the SOC2 pack
[10:42] Call ends
